messages:
morgan: quick proposal — allow `X-Tenant-Tag` header to take precedence over UA-based routing when tenant is on "premium-routing" opt-in. Reason: some clients can't set UA reliably (mobile sdk) but can set tenant tag server-side.

anya: hmm can we trust a plain header? what's spoof protection? :thinking_face:

morgan: good q. plan is: only accept `X-Tenant-Tag` if requests also present a verified `X-Route-Signature` (signed by gateway/key). without signature, UA rules remain. sketch of policy:
```
routing:
  match:
    - header: X-Route-Signature
      verified: true
      effect: allow-tenant-tag-override
    - header: User-Agent
      effect: ua-based-routing
```

sahil: i don't love adding another signature header. how does this interact with auth propagation? e.g., `Authorization` forwarding via private deployment? we need to ensure tenant header can't be used to escalate to reserved capacity or higher quota.

tess: Agreed. We should tie the override to both signature + customer id in token. i.e. verify JWT `sub` matches tenant claim or the signature issuer. Also add a console flag per-tenant: "allow tenant-tag override".

morgan: yes console toggle + rule. telemetry: emit `routing.override_explicit` with fields [tenant_id, route_variant, decision_reason]. we'll add a dashboard row under "Routing decisions" so SRE/product can see how often override fires.

anya: what about fallback? if signature verification fails, and UA points to dedicated pool, do we fallback to hosted? we need deterministic tie-breaker.

sahil: prefer deterministic precedence: 1) signed tenant-tag override 2) signed route header 3) UA-based match 4) default pool. If override fails verification => treat as missing and continue to next.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline queued for branch `feature/tenant-override` (pipeline #421) :rocket:

tess: tests: need unit for header parsing, integration for route selection, and a synthetic load test to ensure batching/caches behave when overrides applied. Also add quota check so requests with override can't bypass reserved capacity quotas.

anya: UX: console should show an auditor-friendly log: who enabled toggle + last 30 days of override decisions. compliance wants that.

morgan: I'll draft an RFC with sample config, API changes (admin toggle + new telemetry event), and rollout plan (canary in eu-west, 1% then 10%). Will post later today. :thumbsup:

sahil: +1 on RFC. also add a lint rule to ensure no wildcard allow for `X-Tenant-Tag` in gateway configs.

morgan: noted. thanks all.
